description: Ask the user for a file or a secret, such as an API key, token or password, without them pasting it into the chat. They answer on a seal.net page: on their computer it opens in their browser by itself; elsewhere a card in their SEAL inbox, which only that inbox answers, or a link anyone holding it can answer. Pass `where_url`, the page where that key is created, and they find it in one click. With `wait:true` you get the path of the saved private file, never the value. Use this instead of "paste your key here" or "upload the file here".

bind.description: kind=secret: where the key will be used, proposed to the person. The page shows it when it does not recognise the key; the person confirms, narrows or removes it. The guard then lets the key out only to these hosts, so never give it for a password you will pass as `password_file`: that file would hold a stand-in.

dir.description: Where to save an answer that comes through a link or a card; created if missing. Default: a private folder in the system's temp folder. A folder you name is ~/Downloads, the working directory or a folder inside one of them, with no hidden folder on the way. An existing file is never overwritten: the new one becomes `name (1).ext`. The page opened on this computer saves where the `seal` CLI does.

from.description: `owner`: a card in the connected user's inbox, which only that inbox answers, from its list: use it when the user may be away from this computer; `anyone`: a link anyone holding it can answer. Without it: the page opens in this computer's browser when there is one, else a card in the connected user's inbox, else the link.

kind.description: `secret`: a password field; `file`: a file; `any`: a secret, or a file when the field is left empty.

request.description: Handle of a request answered through a link: wait for it.

wait.description: Wait for the answer and return the saved path. Where the answer goes through a link and your client cannot show links itself, the link comes back first: show it and the eight words to the user, then call again with `request`.

what.description: What you ask for, as the user reads it: 'Brave API key', 'the call recordings folder'. Required unless `request` is given.

where_url.description: https page where this key is created. The user sees its domain; known services are named, any other domain is marked as given by you.

name: seal_request
title: Ask the user for a file or a secret
